coverage: One bad and one good static YAML example per enabled rule. Every good example is also checked against all twenty rules. No finding is not a complete security assessment. Fixtures stay outside .github/workflows and are never executed. Image digests are illustrative. Selected action tag-to-commit mappings were verified against GitHub API on 2026-11-02.

examples.notes: A moving action tag versus a full commit reference. Review the commit and keep it updated.
Pass untrusted PR text through an environment variable rather than substituting it into shell source.
Broad token write permissions versus the individual contents: read permission.
The bad value is an explicit noncredential demo marker. Findings must not reproduce credential candidates.
Forward one explicitly named secret instead of inheriting every available secret. The called workflow is illustrative.
Exporting the entire secrets context versus forwarding only the required secret.
The good example treats the response as a file and does not execute it. example.invalid is an inert demonstration domain.
Disable HTTPS certificate verification versus keeping certificate checks enabled.
Mutable image tag versus full digest syntax. The digest is illustrative; resolve a real reviewed digest before deploying.

A literal noncredential password marker versus a named secret reference. Reports must omit the literal value. The good image uses an illustrative full digest; resolve a real reviewed digest before deploying.
Public PR eligibility on a self-hosted runner versus a GitHub-hosted runner. Repository approval and isolation settings require separate review.
Privileged PR automation executes the PR head versus the trusted default checkout. This example uses a legacy checkout commit.
An upstream artifact overwrites executable workspace files versus downloading separately and reading data without executing it. Provenance still needs review.
Explicitly including a hidden credential filename versus uploading one allowlisted report. Fixtures contain no credential file.
An explicit writable privileged cache after untrusted PR execution versus restore-only metadata work. Current low-trust trigger defaults are read-only.
Untrusted newlines can inject additional environment-file entries. Remove carriage returns and newlines before writing a single-line value.
An attacker-controlled executable search directory versus an exact allowlist check against an administrator-controlled directory.
Literal comparison text outside the expression produces a truthy string. Put the entire comparison inside one expression.
String contains() permits substring identities, while membership in an explicit JSON array compares complete identities.

Bad uses affected exact version v4.1.2; good pins the commit mapped by the official v4.1.3 tag, verified through GitHub API. The local advisory checker does not infer release versions from unknown SHAs; the existing guard unit tests separately cover the exact v4.1.3 patch boundary. This remains limited to the curated snapshot.
Effective true legacy workflow-command opt-in versus environment-file use; inherited overrides are respected.
Literal privileged Docker option versus reduced capabilities; image digest is illustrative, not verified.
